summary: A person can move a repository's GitHub polling to another member: a top-level stop of the standing observer observer/github/OWNER/REPO, applied on that member, declares the observer stopped, and that member's next pass for any watch it holds declares it again there and polls on from the observer's cursor (#5182)

replay.detail: No graph replay. The stop writes the same intent.desired declaration a host writes when an observer falls unused.

rules.detail: A top-level `stop "observer/github/OWNER/REPO"` is now accepted at parse; it takes no reason. Publication refuses it from any actor but a person with `observer-stop-person-only`; a host's own declarations carry no actor and are unchanged. A top-level observer declaration, and a stop of any other observer, stay refused as before.

compatibility.detail: Mixed-version fleets with the previous release interoperate: the stop's declaration, observer "github/OWNER/REPO" { stop }, is the one every build already writes and folds, so a previous-release member reads it as the observer stopped and drops its cursor row, and reads the re-declaration as another member's, as it does today. A previous-release member refuses the new stop syntax at parse, so a person runs it on a member of this build.

manual.detail: No step is required. To move polling, a person applies the stop on the member that should poll, which needs a watch of the repository there.

recovery.detail: Rolling back leaves the stopped and re-declared observer as ordinary declarations an earlier build reads; only the new stop syntax is refused again.
